extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary staff, and counsel involved in OED proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO Final Order describing disciplinary violations, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions for a registered patent attorney who failed to notify clients, provided misleading information, and neglected entrusted matters. Includes the regulatory basis for discipline and detailed sanctioning and reinstatement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowingly providing false or misleading information to a client (37 C.F.R. §10.23(a) via §10.23(c)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes knowingly providing false or misleading information to the client in connection with the patent, PCT, and trademark applications for which the practitioner was hired to prepare, file, and prosecute before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the stipulation: informing the client 'Everything is fine' when the respondent knew that patent and trademark applications had not been revived; telling the client the Office had mailed correspondence to the practitioner's 'old address' when correspondence was mailed to the practitioner's current address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where the practitioner provided false or misleading information to the client regarding the status of their patent, PCT, and trademark applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (37 C.F.R. §§10.23(b)(4) and 10.23(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where the practitioner provided false or misleading information to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline in connection with its investigation of the practitioner's misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice (37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes behavior such as failing to keep clients informed, providing misleading statements, and neglecting matters that collectively reflect adversely on fitness to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect of entrusted legal matters (37 C.F.R. §10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes neglect of entrusted legal matters, including allowing patent, PCT, and trademark applications to become abandoned or withdrawn without the client's knowledge or consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated misconduct: not taking appropriate corrective action to revive or restore abandoned applications; failing to keep oneself adequately apprised of the status of matters pending before the Office; failing to keep the client timely and accurately informed as to the status of their applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to notify client of correspondence that could significantly affect a matter (37 C.F.R. §10.23(a) via §10.23(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes not notifying the client of correspondence from the Office that could have had a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office when such correspondence was received by the practitioner and a reasonable practitioner would believe under the circumstances the client should be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where practitioner received Office notices (e.g., Notices of Abandonment) but did not inform the client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failing to seek lawful objectives of a client through reasonably available means (37 C.F.R. §10.84(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes failing to seek the lawful objectives of a client through reasonably available means permitted by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where practitioner allowed applications to become abandoned or withdrawn and/or did not seek to revive or restore them, thereby failing to pursue the client's lawful objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdictional authority for discipline (35 U.S.C. §§2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. §§11.20, 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal basis establishing the USPTO Director's jurisdiction to discipline registered practitioners and to approve settlement agreements resolving disciplinary actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as the statutory and regulatory authority for the Director and OED to bring and resolve disciplinary proceedings and to publish disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: suspension, limited recognition, and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreed sanctions in this Final Order: suspension from practice before the USPTO for thirty-six (36) months; limited recognition to practice for 30 days solely to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. §11.58(b); and a thirty-six (36) month period of probation beginning on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order requires compliance with 37 C.F.R. §11.58 and describes the effective dates and scope (limited recognition purpose-limited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition and timing rules (37 C.F.R. §11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing petitions for reinstatement: respondent may file a petition for reinstatement at any time after six (6) months from the date the Final Order is signed requesting reinstatement effective prior to expiration of the 36-month suspension; respondent remains suspended until the OED Director grants reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.60(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the OED Director deems the respondent to have failed conditions during probation, the Director may issue an Order to Show Cause and pursue barring reinstatement or immediate suspension per the procedures set out in the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement procedures and remedial actions (orders to show cause, dissociation of customer numbers/PKI, publication, and costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural tools and remedial consequences used to enforce the Final Order: issuance of Orders to Show Cause with a 15-day response period; forwarding OED materials to the USPTO Director to request barring reinstatement or immediate suspension; dissociation of the respondent's name from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates; prohibition on applying for a Customer Number until reinstated; publication of the Final Order and Notice in the OED Reading Room and Official Gazette; each party bearing its own costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details of the Order to Show Cause process (who issues, where sent, response time), immediate administrative steps (dissociation of credentials), and publicity of the disciplinary action. The Office retains the ability to consider this record in future discipline as an aggravating factor.
